exposure: Women who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection
Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection
Women who tested negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection or had no SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis
cohort: 838,489 women who delivered during the pandemic (March-December 2020) or prepandemic (matched months 2017-2019)
finding: The frequency of adverse pregnancy-related outcomes did not differ between women delivering before compared with during the pandemic, nor between those classified as positive compared with negative for SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy.
mod_finding: The frequency of cesarean birth did not differ significantly between those who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 infection and those classified as testing negative.
